subject.title: Telegram `reason: stopped` wedge still occurs (2026.6.11 & main) — #94008 fix incomplete, root cause #70024

question: Should stop-timeout recovery require each channel owner to guarantee transport termination before the shared gateway discards task state and restarts the account?
rationale: The existing generic recovery path and the requested forced dispatcher destruction have materially different safety properties: the latter addresses a live established poll, while the former can otherwise orphan it before starting another poller.

options.title: Define transport termination first
options.body: Require the Telegram owner to expose a bounded stop operation that destroys the held polling transport, then retain shared restart cleanup behind that guarantee.

options.title: Use generic cleanup only
options.body: Allow the shared gateway to discard stale task state and restart without proving the old transport is gone, accepting possible overlap risk.

options.title: Keep the current retry behavior
options.body: Defer a change until a controlled established-connection reproduction is available, leaving the reported manual gateway-restart recovery requirement in place.

recommendation.title: Define transport termination first
recommendation.body: Require the Telegram owner to expose a bounded stop operation that destroys the held polling transport, then retain shared restart cleanup behind that guarantee.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged adjacent recovery change is the closest current-main ownership signal for deciding the intended stop-timeout recovery contract.
